review_scope: Independent adversarial inspection of artifact source, exact before/after unified patch, candidate01 delta, and accepted design02; no application, compilation, tests, or fixture execution.

source_checks.assessment: Bounded channels precede child spawn; the existing Self cleanup owner is installed immediately after successful spawn, before pipe extraction and worker creation.

Fallible Builder workers preserve fixed typed startup errors and immediately install successful handles. Later local pipes drop before the owner on constructor error; constructed workers remain owned. constructing becomes false only after readiness and browser identity validation.
The Copy close Result is cached after one finalized attempt, including failure, so later close/Drop does not create another cleanup budget.

Partial missing-worker startup cannot create an ACK success. Ordinary ACK handling retains the existing first cleanup deadline and checks elapsed time after receiving a frame. Channel disposal follows ordinary ACK handling and releases blocked reader sends.

Wait, deadline, and forced-kill errors are accumulated rather than bypassing resource cleanup. The second existing 15-second phase starts once and polls actual child status plus present workers; timeout remains failure. Node reaping is assigned only from observed status, with separate worker completion observation.

Only finished handles are joined. Ordinary missing workers and failed joins remain failures. ACK, known browser identity/exited flag, outcome, stderr count, and actual Node exit-code checks remain required for ordinary success.

All cleanup and construction/unwinding Drop diagnostics use ignored best-effort writeln stderr Results. Fixed strings/enums/booleans/counts/status metadata preserve the existing logging boundary; stderr write failure no longer intentionally panics or interrupts Result caching.

No concrete Rust ownership, type inference, Copy-result/status, or shared/mutable borrow inconsistency found by inspection. Formatting-induced nested-if/let-chain changes preserve the prior join conditions.

limits: Source/design acceptance only; no compiler/typecheck or runtime confirmation.

No product, business-session, release, or deployment acceptance is granted.
